description:
tpc-tuning.json is an untracked scratchpad containing two sets of tuning
recommendations generated in a prior AI conversation. The file is malformed
(an AI response is embedded as text between two JSON objects) and is not
integrated into the project. Because the file is intentionally untracked,
implementation must first confirm that the restored scratchpad is present in
the active worktree before relying on the candidate list below.

Treat the scratchpad as an input candidate list, not as design authority.
Databricks table-level Z-ORDER behavior is driven from UnifiedTuning
`table_tunings` columns (`clustering` plus `distribution`) through
`DatabricksAdapter._build_zorder_columns`; there is no supported per-table
`z_ordering_columns` field. The current `platform_optimizations.
z_ordering_columns` lists are global configuration fields and must not be
expanded unless runtime code is shown to consume them for the target path.

Candidate columns from tpc-tuning.json to normalize against the current
Databricks YAML files:

TPC-H candidates:
  lineitem:   l_suppkey, l_shipdate
  orders:     o_orderkey, o_custkey
  customer:   c_nationkey
  supplier:   s_suppkey, s_nationkey
  part:       p_partkey, p_type, p_size

TPC-DS candidates:
  customer:   c_current_addr_sk, c_current_cdemo_sk
  date_dim:   d_year, d_moy
  item:       i_category, i_class
  sales_returns (virtual group): customer_sk, item_sk, store_sk,
                                 promotion_sk, ticket_number
  web_catalog (virtual group):   web_page_sk, web_site_sk, ship_mode_sk

Goal: revalidate the scratchpad, normalize candidates against the current
Databricks YAML baseline, audit only missing candidate columns against actual
TPC-H/TPC-DS query templates, integrate supported columns through the
TableTuning schema, and delete tpc-tuning.json. If no candidates survive the
audit, YAML changes are not required; the correct outcome is to document the
drop decision and remove the scratchpad.

anti_patterns.why: the TableTuning schema does not support them and Databricks builds Z-ORDER columns from clustering plus distribution.

anti_patterns.dont: add z-ordering columns based solely on the JSON recommendations without validating query usage
anti_patterns.why: untested tuning columns waste compute on optimize operations without improving query times.

anti_patterns.dont: delete tpc-tuning.json before w3 is complete
anti_patterns.why: it is the only record of the recommendations being evaluated.
DuckDB doesn't support Z-ordering; those files use ORDER BY and are independently maintained.

anti_patterns.dont: resolve the "sales_returns" and "web_catalog" virtual table names in the JSON to real columns by guessing
anti_patterns.why: the JSON was generated by an AI with no access to actual query templates; check the query files directly.

anti_patterns.dont: search benchbox/core/tpch/queries/ or benchbox/core/tpcds/queries/ as directories
anti_patterns.why: runtime query templates live under benchbox/_binaries/.../templates.

preserves.behavior: Existing Databricks platform_optimizations z_ordering_columns and table_tunings partitioning/clustering/distribution columns - the audit must not remove or reorder any column that is currently there.
The ALL-CAPS naming convention for column names in Databricks YAML files.
examples/tunings/duckdb/ - these files must not be touched; DuckDB uses ORDER BY not Z-ordering.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/tpcds/c_tools.py:DSQGenBinary - reuse; stages bundled TPC-DS query_templates/query_variants for dsqgen
benchbox/core/tpch/queries.py:QGenBinary.generate - reuse; points DSS_QUERY at bundled TPC-H query/variant templates
benchbox/core/tuning/interface.py:TableTuning - reuse; supported per-table fields are partitioning, clustering, distribution, and sorting
benchbox/platforms/databricks/adapter.py:DatabricksAdapter._build_zorder_columns - reuse; Databricks Z-ORDER columns come from clustering plus distribution
benchbox/utils/tpc_compilation.py:get_tpc_templates_dir - reuse; locates bundled TPC-H/TPC-DS template roots

verifications.description: Scratchpad is gone and Databricks YAML diff is whitespace-clean
tpc-tuning.json no longer exists in the working tree

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.cli.config import ConfigManager; cm=ConfigManager(); [cm.load_unified_tuning_config(p, 'databricks') for p in ('examples/tunings/databricks/tpch_tuned.yaml', 'examples/tunings/databricks/tpcds_tuned.yaml')]; print('ok')"
verifications.description: Databricks tuning YAML still loads through the unified tuning loader
DuckDB tuning examples were not modified

verifications.command: rg -n 'tpc-tuning' benchbox/ examples/ tests/ docs/ || echo 'no references'
verifications.description: No codebase reference to tpc-tuning.json remains
Databricks TPC tuning examples retain accepted columns and reject low-evidence candidates

work_units.notes:
Confirm tpc-tuning.json exists in the implementation worktree before
using the description's candidate list. Run:
  uv run -- python -m json.tool tpc-tuning.json

Expected result: the command fails because the file contains two JSON
objects separated by an AI-response sentence. Record a compact summary
of the checked path, file size/line count, parse failure, and candidate
groups in the PR body or DONE notes. Do not commit raw stdout and do not
commit tpc-tuning.json.

Normalize the candidate list against:
  examples/tunings/databricks/tpch_tuned.yaml
  examples/tunings/databricks/tpcds_tuned.yaml

For each candidate, classify it as already covered by table_tunings
partitioning/clustering/distribution, missing and audit-needed, or
unsupported/virtual and requiring query-template resolution. Do not add
duplicate columns that are already represented in table_tunings.
work_units.summary: Revalidate scratchpad evidence and current Databricks tuning baseline

work_units.notes:
For each TPC-H candidate that w0 classified as missing from the current
Databricks table_tunings baseline:

Search the 22 TPC-H query templates in
benchbox/_binaries/tpc-h/templates/queries/ for WHERE / JOIN / GROUP BY
/ ORDER BY uses of that column. Also account for runtime variants that
replace a base query, especially query 15a in
benchbox/_binaries/tpc-h/templates/variants/, because QGenBinary points
DSS_QUERY at these bundled template directories.

Acceptance criterion: >= 3 queries use the column selectively -> keep it.
Document findings in a simple table (column | query count | keep/drop).
work_units.summary: Audit TPC-H query files for candidate column usage in predicates and joins

work_units.notes:
Same methodology as w1 but for TPC-DS. Search the 99 bundled templates
in benchbox/_binaries/tpc-ds/templates/query_templates/ plus any selected
variants in benchbox/_binaries/tpc-ds/templates/query_variants/. DSQGen
stages these directories at runtime via DSQGenBinary; do not search the
nonexistent benchbox/core/tpcds/queries/ directory.

Candidate columns to check:
  customer:       c_current_addr_sk, c_current_cdemo_sk
  date_dim:       d_year, d_moy
  item:           i_category, i_class
  sales_returns:  the JSON uses a virtual table name; resolve to the real
                  per-table columns (ss_customer_sk, ss_store_sk,
                  ss_promo_sk, ss_ticket_number, etc.)
  web_catalog:    resolve virtual table to real columns across
                  web_page, web_site, ship_mode tables

Acceptance criterion same as w1 (>= 3 queries). Document findings.
work_units.summary: Audit TPC-DS query files for candidate column usage in predicates and joins

work_units.notes:
Files to modify:
  examples/tunings/databricks/tpch_tuned.yaml
  examples/tunings/databricks/tpcds_tuned.yaml

For each column that passed the acceptance criterion:
  - Add it under the correct table_tunings.<TABLE>.clustering list,
    unless the existing table pattern clearly makes distribution the
    correct representation.
  - Continue the existing order numbering within that tuning type.
  - Match the existing ALL-CAPS naming convention used in those files
  - Keep the ordering: date/partition columns first, then FK/join columns,
    then filter columns

Do NOT add a per-table z_ordering_columns field; TableTuning only
supports partitioning, clustering, distribution, and sorting. Do NOT
expand platform_optimizations.z_ordering_columns unless a targeted code
read proves that global list is consumed for this Databricks table path
and the verification covers that behavior.

Do NOT add columns that failed the criterion. Do NOT modify
examples/tunings/duckdb/ - DuckDB uses ORDER BY, not Z-ordering.
work_units.summary: Integrate accepted columns into Databricks table_tunings

work_units.notes:
The file is untracked (confirmed via git status), so deletion requires only:
  rm tpc-tuning.json

Before deleting, search the codebase to confirm nothing imports or loads it:
  rg -n "tpc-tuning" benchbox/ examples/ tests/ docs/

If any reference exists, update it first.
work_units.summary: Delete tpc-tuning.json and verify nothing references it
